title: SLI curve fitting and dashboard experiment notes
content:
Summary:
This is a working doc for an experiment to: (1) define compact, cost-aware SLIs that reflect user-perceived latency and model-quality risk; (2) try a curve-fitting approach to map metric distributions into an SLI curve instead of brittle thresholds; (3) prototype a small dashboard surface and trace anchors for efficient investigation. The goal is a trial during the next canary rollout (Q1 release window).

Why curve-fitting?
- Threshold SLIs (p95 < 200ms) are easy but brittle for multitenant inference with bursty token flows and KV cache effects.
- We want an SLI that degrades smoothly and is interpretable for oncall and product stakeholders, and that can be tied to token-cost implications.

Goals for the experiment
- Produce 1 canonical SLI definition per persona: operator SLI (investigation-first), developer SLI (regression alerting), product SLI (user-facing latency).
- Implement curve-fitting pipeline for one node pool (gpu-dedicated-eu-west) and a single model family (redwood-opena-v1) with KV-prefetch toggles.
- Build lightweight dashboard with 6 panels and trace jump links.
- Measure false alerts/alert fatigue vs baseline threshold SLI across 4 weeks.

Metric primitives and definitions (canonical names we will instrument)
- token_ttf_ms: time from request receive to first token emitted (ms).
- token_emit_rate_tokens_per_s: instantaneous token output rate (tokens/s) measured per request-window.
- kv_cache_hit_rate: fraction of requests where prefix KV cache returned usable entries (0-1).
- inference_latency_p50_p95_p99_ms: quantiles of end-to-end inference time per request.
- effective_batch_size: tokens batched per inference kernel submission (weighted).
- cost_per_token_usd: derived cost attribution per token for GPU cycle allocation.
- session_failure_rate: fraction of requests with model error/hallucination flags (post-filter).

Curve-fitting SLI approach (sketch)
- For each metric M (e.g., token_ttf_ms), compute daily distribution vector D = [p10,p25,p50,p75,p90,p95,p99].
- Fit a monotonic logistic or power-law curve f(q) mapping quantile->value: f(q) = a / (1 + exp(-b*(q-c))) + d  OR simpler power fit v = alpha * q^beta + gamma.
- Convert curve to an SLI score S in [0,100] by normalizing against baseline historical percentiles and cost budget: S(M) = 100 * (1 - (AreaUnderCurve_degradation / baseline_auc_threshold)).
- Compose multiple metrics into a single composite SLI using weighted geometric mean to penalize large degradations: S_total = prod_i S(M_i)^{w_i} where sum(w_i)=1, weights set by persona.
- Rationale: geometric mean ensures a single very bad signal drives the composite down quickly.

Practical fitting details and heuristics
- Use 28-day rolling baseline for parameter initialization; re-fit weekly with robust loss (Huber) to avoid large outliers dominating.
- Maintain an emergency fallback: if we detect insufficient samples for a window (e.g., < 200 requests/day for a cohort) default back to threshold SLI for that cohort.
- Use quantile sketches (t-digest) to produce D without storing full histograms.
- Store fitted parameters (a,b,c,d) in time-series so we can backtest SLI decisions historically.

Dashboard experiment design (panels and intent)
- Panel 1: Composite SLI (S_total) with burn-down bands (green/yellow/red) and show deviation from baseline. Drill link -> trace anchor.
- Panel 2: token_ttf quantile curve overlay: historical baseline curve vs today curve (plot continuous q->value).
- Panel 3: kv_cache_hit_rate heatmap by tenant shard and by hour (shows prefetch/cold periods).
- Panel 4: effective_batch_size vs cost_per_token scatter with kernel utilization heatmap (to detect batching regressions).
- Panel 5: trace-sampled request waterfall for slow tails: show span durations, model forward time, kernel wait time, kv lookup time.
- Panel 6: Alert cadence and hitlist: list of triggered SLI alerts, linked Jira keys, oncall notes.

Trace anchoring and correlation notes
- Add trace tag: trace.anchor_session_id = hashed(session_id) to stitch multi-request sessions.
- Span-level tags to add: span.kv_prefetch = true/false, span.kernel_batch_size = n, span.kernel_model_variant = quantized|fp16|int8.
- For tokenized inference, capture token-range spans: span.token_produce[start:end] so we can correlate tail latency to token positions.
- Sampling strategy: severity-weighted sampling: always capture 100% of requests where token_ttf > p99 and sample 0.1% baseline requests. Budget target: < 30GB/day trace storage for the trial.

Investigation-first UX flow (oncall play)
- S_total alert fires -> open panel shows top contributing metrics (shap-like breakdown).
- Drill to token_ttf curve and tenant heatmap -> shortlist tenants > p95 deviation.
- Jump to trace jump link for a representative slow request (auto-sampled by severity).
- Quick triage checklist: check kv_cache_heatmap, check recent model variant rollout, check kernel saturation and batch size, check infra CPU steal / time sync.

Sampling and query-cost considerations
- We will track query-cost impact of added telemetry: estimated trace bytes per sample * samples/day -> cost. Keep probe budget adjustable per node pool.
- For dashboard panels with heavy-cardinality (tenant x model x region), implement TTL-based snapshotting: full enumeration every 10 minutes, roll-up hourly aggregates otherwise.

Rollout checklist (canary -> staged -> global)
- Instrumentation: finalize span tags and metric names (owner: Ava).
- Baseline: collect 2 weeks of baseline data with sampling ON but no alerting (owner: Morgan).
- Backtest: run SLI computation retrospectively on 28 days to tune weights/threshold polish (owner: Ravi).
- Canary: enable alerts for a small tenant cohort (5%). Monitor alert noise for 7 days.
- Staged: 25% cohort for 14 days.
- Global: enable for all tenants, continue weekly re-fit cadence.

Open questions / unknowns
- How to map S_total to SLA penalties? product wants a crisp mapping; ops wants a graded one. Need legal/product discussion (JIRA-OBS-892).
- Weighting strategy for composite SLI: subjective today. Propose workshop to set weights by persona and feature (deadline next week).
- Model-quality signal integration: session_failure_rate needs better instrumentation (post-filter ground truth is delayed). Should we run a light online significance test?
- Cost per token attribution correctness at multi-model fanout. Need finance input on GPU amortization model.

Immediate next steps
- (Ravi) Draft PR that adds span tags and exposes token_ttf_ms as a top-level metric (PR: telemetry#412). Target: 2026-02-20.
- (Ava) Synthetic probe: implement traffic generator that warms KV prefixes and produces controlled tail events. Target: 2026-02-25.
- (Morgan) Dashboard skeleton in Grafana with the six panels above, linked to the trace jump-playbook. Target: 2026-03-05.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally light on final numbers; the work here is to get a reproducible fitting pipeline and an investigation flow. Expect multiple iterations.
- Please comment directly in this Drive doc or link related investigation notes. Use slack thread #observability-sli-curves for quick syncs.

Attachments / smaller artifacts we will create (follow-ups)
- simple Jupyter notebook: fit_examples.ipynb that shows logistic vs power-law fit on p10..p99 vectors.
- t-digest ingestion snippet: tdigest-ingest.go for telemetry daemon.
- Grafana JSON dashboards (draft).

Versioning and audit
- Save fitted parameter snapshots daily to timeseries table telemetry.sli_fits, tag with git-commit and rollout tag so we can reproduce exact behavior at alert time.

Owner and reviewers
- Doc owner: Ravi K. Patel
- Reviewers: Ava Chen (instrumentation), Morgan Alvarez (dashboards), Diego Ruiz (SRE)

-- end of doc --
